proposed_contract_delta.external_identity_recovery: Configured IdP owns credential recovery; portal offers the configured IdP sign-in/recovery path and requires fresh authentication before portal access. If the returned issuer+subject is unchanged, resolve the same external participant and retain current unexpired grants, then recheck issuer status, participant state, grant revision/epoch, expiry and field/action ceilings. Recovery alone creates no identity or grant. Do not require revoke/reinvite for an unchanged principal changing email/contact endpoint. If issuer+subject changes, never auto-transfer grants: require an explicit audited rebind under a separately authorized, provider-independent proof policy or treat the identity as new and require fresh party invitation and grant.
proposed_contract_delta.contact_endpoint_change: The portal exposes a typed command owned by ExternalParticipant/Invitation application orchestration and delegates endpoint normalization, verification challenge and revision storage to existing internal/domains/contact (CONTACT-001/002). Proposed additive API: UpdateExternalContactEndpointRequest{participant_ref,company_ref,expected_endpoint_revision,new_endpoint,purpose,challenge_ref,idempotency_key}; response UpdateExternalContactEndpointResponse{endpoint_revision,endpoint_update_receipt,superseded_invitation_refs}. Verify proposed endpoint under Contact owner policy; same-subject contact changes retain valid current grants. A successful endpoint revision change supersedes only unaccepted invitations bound to the old endpoint revision. It does not revoke grants or force reinvitation of the same participant. New invitations bind the new endpoint revision.
proposed_contract_delta.existing_grants: A verified email/contact endpoint change for the same issuer+subject updates contact evidence only and leaves existing unexpired grants in place, subject to fresh authentication and ordinary current grant rechecks. A different issuer+subject is never silently mapped or granted prior authority: use an explicitly audited rebind policy with provider-independent proof if separately authorized, otherwise require a fresh invitation/grant. Preserve existing audit receipts and authored conversation/document attribution; recipient exposure always checks current grant.
proposed_contract_delta.abuse_and_recovery: Credential recovery and MFA/password recovery remain at the configured IdP. The portal does not store credential or recovery secrets or mint an alternate recovery credential. After IdP recovery require fresh authentication; neutral handling of unknown/unauthorized portal participants; no raw authorization codes or invite tokens in URL history/referrer/logs. Endpoint verification challenges use Contact owner digest-only, single-use, expiry and attempt/rate controls. Failed/expired/replayed endpoint challenges and stale revisions create no endpoint/grant change; preserve required sanitized security evidence under its owner.
proposed_contract_delta.endpoint_revision_api: UpdateExternalContactEndpoint command is scoped to the authenticated external participant and company party grant plus current endpoint revision. Idempotency digest binds participant_ref, company_ref, expected_endpoint_revision, normalized new_endpoint, purpose and challenge_ref. Same-key/same-payload retry returns the same endpoint revision receipt and superseded-invitation set; same-key/changed-payload conflicts; stale expected_endpoint_revision returns current revision only to an authorized caller and makes no update. Concurrent endpoint updates have one CAS winner; only its newly-bound endpoint revision is used to issue future invites.

After successful fresh authentication, same issuer+subject resolves the existing external participant. Display a represented-party picker only after live grant checks; if no active grant, show that access needs a current invitation. Never show cached party/work/request/document data until current authorization succeeds.

Contact update clearly shows current and proposed masked endpoint, verification state and pending authorized approval when policy requires it. Success states the new endpoint revision, that active same-subject grants remain governed by their current validity, and that only unaccepted old-revision invitations are superseded. A same-subject contact change does not require revoke/reinvite. Any changed issuer+subject enters an explicit audited rebind policy or a fresh invitation path; no automatic grant transfer.
